title: Veritas user requirements
note: Severity and likelihood are rated 1 (low) to 3 (high); the generator derives the risk class. Every requirement lists the automated tests that verify it, by test ID. Changing a requirement, its rating or its tests is reviewed like code.

requirements.requirement: Only a person with a valid session sees the workspace or any controlled data; no request header, cookie other than the session, or unknown identity grants access.
requirements.hazard: Someone without an account reads or changes controlled records.
requirements.control: Opaque server-side sessions validated on every request; the workspace layout checks the session on the server.

requirements.requirement: Sign-in needs the person's password and a code from their authenticator app; a correct password alone opens no session.
requirements.hazard: A stolen or guessed password gives full access.
requirements.control: Two-step verification for everyone; pending sign-in token valid five minutes; secrets stored encrypted.

requirements.requirement: Repeated wrong passwords or codes are refused for 15 minutes, without revealing whether an account exists.
requirements.hazard: Passwords or codes are guessed online.
requirements.control: Failure counts per email, per address and per identity from the identity audit trail.

requirements.requirement: What a person may do follows the permissions of their organisation role, never a job title or department.
requirements.hazard: A person acts beyond their role.
requirements.control: Persisted role permissions checked by every route; the interface follows the same permissions.

requirements.requirement: Passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes and never logged.
requirements.hazard: A database or log copy reveals passwords.
requirements.control: Argon2id with a unique salt; password material excluded from logs.

requirements.requirement: Sessions expire, can be revoked, and stop working when the person, membership or organisation is deactivated.
requirements.hazard: A former member keeps access.
requirements.control: Session validation re-checks identity, membership and organisation status.

requirements.requirement: An administrator invites a person with one organisation role; the person sets their own password from a single-use 30-minute link; every step is audited.
requirements.hazard: Accounts are created without trace, or someone else knows the password.
requirements.control: Atomic invitation with audit rows; hashed single-use credential tokens.

requirements.requirement: An administrator can reset another member's two-step verification with a reason, never their own, and the reset is audited.
requirements.hazard: A lost phone locks someone out, or a reset weakens an account without trace.
requirements.control: Reset needs users.update and a reason; refused for oneself and across organisations; audited in both trails.

requirements.requirement: One organisation never sees or changes another organisation's documents, training, audit entries, people or notifications.
requirements.hazard: Confidential records leak between customers.
requirements.control: Tenant-scoped predicates, composite tenant keys and row-level security for the application database role.

requirements.requirement: A document moves draft, in review, approved, effective, superseded or obsolete only through the allowed transitions, each audited.
requirements.hazard: A document becomes effective without review and approval.
requirements.control: Lifecycle transitions checked on every route with status-guarded updates.

requirements.requirement: Review, approval, release and retirement are each signed by an assigned person; the author cannot release their own version.
requirements.hazard: One person writes and releases a controlled document alone.
requirements.control: Assignment checks and segregation of duties on review, approval and release.

requirements.requirement: Releasing a version makes it effective and supersedes the previously effective version in the same transaction.
requirements.hazard: Two versions are in force at once.
requirements.control: Release and supersession in one transaction with count checks.

requirements.requirement: An open revision can be withdrawn with a reason; the effective version stays in force and revision numbers are never reused.
requirements.hazard: Withdrawing a revision removes the version in force.
requirements.control: Withdrawal touches only the revision and its open review route.

requirements.requirement: Every stored file is checked against its SHA-256 when it is read or signed; a mismatch is refused.
requirements.hazard: A file is altered in storage and served or signed as genuine.
requirements.control: Hash recorded at upload, verified on every read and before signing.

requirements.requirement: Readers get the effective version by default, exactly as stored; any other version is marked as an uncontrolled copy of its status.
requirements.hazard: Someone works from an outdated or unapproved version believing it is in force.
requirements.control: Controlled-copy service; a PDF that cannot be stamped is not served.

requirements.requirement: Files are uploaded straight to private storage under a key reserved in the uploader's organisation; another organisation's key is refused.
requirements.hazard: A file lands in, or is claimed from, another organisation's storage.
requirements.control: Server-reserved tenant keys; presigned write-only upload; hash re-checked on read-back.

requirements.requirement: Each signature needs the signer's own password and records printed name, role, meaning, time and the SHA-256 of the signed file, together with its audit row.
requirements.hazard: A signature cannot be attributed to a person or to the exact content signed.
requirements.control: Signature service with password re-entry, written in the same transaction as the state change.

requirements.requirement: Signatures cannot be changed or deleted, by the application or the database owner.
requirements.hazard: A signature is altered after the fact.
requirements.control: Append-only trigger on the signature table.

requirements.requirement: Failed signing attempts are audited, and after five wrong passwords in 15 minutes signing is paused.
requirements.hazard: A signer's password is guessed through a stolen session.
requirements.control: Failed attempts recorded and counted per signer.

requirements.requirement: When a version becomes effective, every active member of the document's training departments is assigned that version, and open training on earlier versions is closed.
requirements.hazard: People work to a new version they were never trained on.
requirements.control: Assignment inside the release transaction, audited.

requirements.requirement: A trainee completes training by signing their own assignment as read and understood, only while that version is effective.
requirements.hazard: Training is recorded for someone else, or against a version no longer in force.
requirements.control: Assignee and permission checks; signature on the version's hash; status-guarded completion.

requirements.requirement: People allowed to see everyone's training see a matrix of people and documents showing open and completed training on the newest version.
requirements.hazard: Gaps in training go unnoticed.
requirements.control: Matrix built from the tenant-scoped training list.

requirements.requirement: Every regulated change writes an audit entry in the same transaction; nobody, including the database owner, can change or delete audit entries.
requirements.hazard: Changes happen without trace, or the trace is rewritten.
requirements.control: Mandatory audit writes; append-only triggers; the application role has no update or delete right.

requirements.requirement: Reviewers see each audit entry with who acted and what changed (before and after), limited to their organisation.
requirements.hazard: Inspectors and reviewers cannot reconstruct what happened.
requirements.control: Audit review screen deriving field changes from stored payloads.

requirements.requirement: The audit review can be exported as a PDF stating who exported it, when and with which filters; the export itself is audited.
requirements.hazard: Exported audit evidence cannot be attributed or is incomplete without saying so.
requirements.control: Audited PDF export with header, numbered pages and an explicit cut-off note.

requirements.requirement: Unexpected errors never reveal internal details to the browser or logs; responses with controlled data are not cached.
requirements.hazard: Error messages or caches expose internal or controlled data.
requirements.control: Fixed error responses with a correlation ID; no-store on regulated reads.

requirements.requirement: Pages and API responses carry baseline security headers, and the framework is not advertised.
requirements.hazard: Common browser attacks (framing, content sniffing) succeed.
requirements.control: Security headers in the application configuration.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration seed never runs against production data.
requirements.source: Roadmap Phase 0 (seed refuses in production), DEC-056
requirements.hazard: Fabricated records enter production.
requirements.control: Seed refuses by default and always in production.
